brief.goal: a one-stage 3D-printed planetary gearbox on a NEMA 17 stepper: a 41x41mm square printed housing with an internal 27-tooth ring gear, a 9-tooth sun pinion pressed on the motor shaft, three 9-tooth planets on a printed carrier that is the output (module 1.2, 4:1), all clamped to the motor by four M3 threaded rods with nuts
brief.design: Compact, functional motor-accessory look: crisp square housing with small 0.5 mm chamfers on outside edges and flat faces that sit flush with the NEMA 17 face. Rotating parts get slightly softer edges and generous running gaps so printed surfaces never rub. No decoration; walls read solid rather than minimal.

housing.title: Gearbox housing with ring gear
housing.spec: Square printed block that bolts onto the NEMA 17 face. A thin floor at the bottom sits on the motor. Above the floor, a 27-tooth internal involute ring gear (module 1.2, 20° pressure angle, small backlash) is cut around a round cavity, and the gear teeth run the full ring width. Above the ring is a round pocket that the planet carrier spins in. A thick top wall closes the box and carries the output shaft. Four clearance holes run the full height at the motor's 31 mm screw pattern so threaded rods can pass from the motor to nuts on the top face.

contract.name: Gearbox housing
contract.summary: 41×41 square housing, open cavity with a 27T m1.2 internal ring gear above a thin floor, carrier pocket above it, thick top wall for the output; four full-height M3 rod holes on a 31 mm square, nuts seat on top.

carrier.title: Planet carrier (output)
carrier.spec: Round printed disc that spins in the housing pocket above the ring gear and is the gearbox output. Its underside carries three planet seats spaced evenly at 120 degrees on the sun-planet mesh radius, and the planets hang below it. The top face runs against the underside of the housing top wall and carries the output hub at its centre.
